observations: Photo 0 shows a wooden double-decker bed frame with a ladder on the right side, placed outdoors on a concrete surface. The frame is reddish-brown with visible wear, chipped paint, and some exposed wood. The top and bottom bunks have slatted bases. The headboard and footboard have vertical slats. The ladder is attached to the side of the frame.

Photo 1 shows the same bed frame from a front-facing angle, with the ladder still attached. The frame appears slightly tilted. The paint is chipped, especially on the lower front leg. The slats on both bunks are visible. A metal object (possibly a ladder or frame) leans against the wall in the background.
No brand or model is visible on the bed frame in either photo.
The bed frame appears to be made of wood, likely particle board or softwood, given the chipping and wear.
The dimensions are not visible in the photos, but the seller claims 3.5 by 6 feet.
